paragraph: In *ବୃନ୍ଦାବନର ଶେଷଧୂପ (Brundabanara Sheshadhupa)*, Bijay Kumar Satapathy’s dramatization of a story by Mahapatra Nilamani Sahu, a crow calls outside Raghu’s home while Subhadra brings his medicine. Later, devotional singing comes from another room; a radio bulletin enters near the close.[^nilamani-stage] The printed play asks us to imagine listeners as well as speakers: a household connected to a world beyond its walls.
footnote: [^nilamani-stage]: Bijay Kumar Satapathy, dramatization of Mahapatra Nilamani Sahu’s story, in Bauribandhu Kar (ed.), [*Sahityasadhak Mohapatra Nilamani Sahu* (2004)](https://new.odiabibhaba.in/en/books/sahityasadhak-mahapatra-nilamani-sahu), pp. 197–198, 204, 211.
editorial_value: Adds a particular dramatic household and the sources of sound around it. Keep the existing Amada scene; avoid another abstract adaptation introduction or a plot synopsis.
